David / Grace / Akira — thanks for the report and logs. Initial findings from a quick triage:

- Correlation: the client freezes line up exactly with a short autoscaler-driven worker handoff on the dedicated pool serving Maple Health (visible in the metrics snapshot). At the same time we see a transient proxy keepalive reset in the upstream (tcp FIN/RST events in the trace).
- Behavior: during the handoff the server continues to accept the connection but our chunked transfer layer temporarily queues outgoing frames until the new worker establishes the KV cache and the model warmstart finishes; queued chunks are flushed in a burst, which looks like a long pause followed by a catch-up of tokens.
- Error spikes: a small percentage of connections saw a 5xx due to a timeout in the handoff path until the retry logic kicked in.

Immediate mitigations we can push now (low-risk):
1) disable aggressive worker rebalancing for the Maple Health dedicated pool for the next 90 minutes (will prevent handoffs during their pilot).
2) flip the proxy keepalive to a longer interval for their route (30s -> 120s) to reduce mid-stream resets.
3) if they accept a temporary fallback, switch them to the smaller-but-stable model variant (gpt-small-redwood) for the demo — slightly higher latency but no warmstart delays.

I've attached a short capture (maplehealth-metrics-20260930.csv) and extracted the tcp trace into ws-session-1234.log for reference. I can be on the 10:30 PT call and run the mitigation changes if we get approval.

Next steps: David — please confirm which mitigation(s) Akira wants. I will prepare a postmortem and a permanent fix: reduce handoff IO blocking and implement streaming drain semantics that avoid queuing entire frames during worker swaps.

-M
Marissa Cole
Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
